intro: Here’s your {weeks}-week Instagram and TikTok strategy for {release}. We’ve built a personalised guide to what you should post and when. Don’t hesitate to use your own ideas too. A personal touch always lands.

modules.title: Top posting tips
modules.html:
{intro}

Timing

Check your Instagram analytics to see when your audience is active. Timing posts is key to the best engagement.

SmartLink

Use a SmartLink in your bio so fans find your music on every platform with a single click.

Profile pic

Keep the same profile picture across every social account. Consistency is key.

Stories

Update your story regularly. More content means more attention and engagement.

modules.title: IG basics: do and don’t
modules.html:
Links
Don’t

Long links ruin your bio’s aesthetic. Shorten them or use your Ditto SmartLink.

Do

A SmartLink looks tidy and takes fans to their preferred platform from one link. We can provide one for you.

Highlights
Don’t

Highlights with no theme look messy, disordered and unappealing.

Do

Named, themed highlights give your audience more insight into who you are as an artist and a person.

Profile picture
Don’t

Blurry, unclear or unrelated pictures discourage people from engaging.

Do

A strong, consistent aesthetic is far more appealing to potential followers.

Bio
Don’t

A line of plain text looks boring and gets skipped.

Do

Say who you are and when your music is out. A well-structured bio with a few emojis catches the eye.

Aesthetics. Standing out on Instagram is essential. A strong, maintained look for your feed builds your brand and overall image. Try black and white, a consistent filter, or a white border.

modules.title: How to: Reels
modules.html:
Reels is one of the best channels to reach new people and grow your audience. Short-form video is everywhere, so it has to be part of your strategy.

  • Keep it simple, fun and share it to your feed so your core fanbase sees it.
  • Be yourself. The best-performing Reels let your personality shine through.
  • Use a few relevant hashtags. Four to six is enough.
  • Add a call to action: ‘Remix my reel’, ‘Flip this sample’.
  • Go with what’s trending. Popular audio and ideas reach new fans.
  • Collaborate with similar artists to reach the audience most likely to enjoy your sound.

Cover song

Your own spin on a popular song, with the right hashtags, reaches a brand new audience.

Remix

Attach your name to content that’s already getting attention. Add your own flair.

Comedy

Light-hearted, relatable posts put your personality front and centre.

Call to action

Content your audience can remix: ‘Producers, sample this sound.’

modules.title: Posting to your feed
modules.html:
Your feed is the most important part of the campaign. It’s where all your content ideas come to life. Before you hit share:

  • Tag the location of the photo.
  • Tag people involved: featured artists, producers, promoters.
  • Tag your DSPs and distribution platforms: Spotify, Apple Music, Ditto.
  • Proof-read and prepare your caption. No misspelt words, nicely formatted.
  • Include some relevant hashtags.

Acoustic videos

Show off your talent in an intimate, stripped-back format.

Release artwork

Share your artwork and tell fans where to hear it.

Press shots

Simple and effective, a must-have on your feed.

Music video clips

Teasers from your video create hype.

Live photos

The best shots and videos from your latest gig.

Behind the scenes

A sneak peek into how things operate.

modules.title: How to: Stories
modules.html:
Stories are often the first thing people check when they open the app, so always have something there for them. Include stickers and your location, tag anyone involved, and keep captions succinct.

Highlights let you curate what your audience sees before they check your feed: live shows, fan activity, press and reviews.

Fan content

Reciprocate the effort your fans give you.

Ask me anything

Take questions and open up to your fans.

Live videos

A quick snippet gives a real taste of what you’re about.

Now playing

Interact and network with artists in your scene.

Wallpapers

A fun bit of content for your biggest fans.

Polls

A quick, easy way to get your fans’ opinion.

modules.title: TikTok basics: do and don’t
modules.html:
Don’t

Load up on broad hashtags like #fyp and #viral. It kills retention by showing your content to the wrong people.

Do

Use the caption strategically to give context to your video.

Don’t

Focus on numbers. Virality doesn’t translate into long-term listeners and fans.

Do

Plan content in advance and post consistently to keep momentum.

Don’t

Simply promote with ‘stream my song’. Direct pitching rarely works. Focus on emotional connection.

Do

Engage with commenters and use comments to create new videos.

Don’t

Force yourself to chase trends.

Do

Test what works for your style and personality. Embrace your uniqueness.

modules.title: Short-form video
modules.html:
Emotional hook

Let your audience into the emotional core of the track. One genuine line before the music hits can land harder than polished production.

Rinse and repeat

Use {release} as the soundtrack of your campaign, as much as possible. Every new piece of content with your track is a new chance to reach the right fans.

Test and repurpose

Try different parts of the audio and different captions to see what lands. Apps like ReelRise and Trendtok help spot what works.

Plan ahead, film in batches

Think two or three campaigns ahead, then film content in batches so you can focus on the music.

Behind the scenes

Studio, rehearsal, the 2am bowl of cereal.

Stitch a comment

Turn comments into content.

Personal anecdotes

Stories only you can tell.

Underdog reality

The honest version of where you are.

Striking visuals

One frame that stops the scroll.

Track origin story

Where the song came from.

modules.title: Community channels
modules.html:
Social apps are building their own direct, inbox-level channels. Think of them as a mailing list or fan group chat: tease content, promote merch and shows, share exclusives.

Instagram Broadcast Channels

A one-to-many group chat with voice notes, polls, prompts and collaborator channels, deeply tied into DMs and Stories.

TikTok Bulletin Boards

A mini broadcast newsletter rather than a place for two-way feedback. Polls, quick text posts, images and links in a lightweight feed.

  • Teasers and pre-save nudges. Time-sensitive sneak peeks for those most invested in your music.
  • Livestream reminders. Tell your community when you’re going live, and give them a reason to join early.
  • Behind the scenes. Daily check-ins, bloopers, ‘here’s what I’m working on’.
  • Exclusive access. Early plays, insider updates and private thoughts that never hit the main grid.

modules.title: Worldbuilding for your campaign
modules.html:
Worldbuilding immerses people in your music by creating a cohesive ‘world’ around {release}. Build a consistent look or idea that represents the vibe or mood of the project, and translate it visually by connecting imagery, fonts, colours and visuals.

Eccentric

Bold type, collage, unexpected colour.

Nostalgic

Film grain, warm tones, found objects.

Grungy

High contrast, black and white, texture.
